Your task: identify concrete issues **in the changed code**. Every
finding must:

- Cite a **real file path and line number** from the diff you were shown.
  Do NOT invent file paths. Do NOT invent line numbers.
- Be **specific** — describe the actual problem in the changed lines.
  Say "new query on line 42 uses f-string interpolation instead of
  parameterized query" — not "the code has issues."
- Have a `severity` of `low`, `medium`, `high`, or `critical`.
- Have a `kind` of `bug`, `security`, `quality`, `missing`, or `design`.
- Come with a one-line `fix_sketch`.

**Banned phrasing.** Do NOT use these in any finding:

- "Add tests", "add unit tests", "improve test coverage"
- "Set up CI/CD", "add CI/CD"
- "Add documentation", "improve docs"
- "Improve code quality", "follow best practices"
- "LGTM", "looks good to me" (the verdict is decided separately)

**Syntax errors are special — do not claim one unless you are certain.**
The files have already been parsed successfully by the indexer. Multi-line
expressions (closing `)` on a continuation line) are valid Python. If you
really believe there's a syntax error, quote the full expression.

**Default values — verify before claiming.** When describing a bug
involving default parameter values, quote the exact function signature.

If you find no issues in the changed code, return zero findings. An
empty findings list is a valid answer — it means the PR is clean.

Your output MUST be valid JSON matching the schema provided.

PR title: Allow per-team sub-folders for exported reports
</untrusted_96653c8ffc9a>

Verified findings (4):
<untrusted_96653c8ffc9a source="findings">
[0] high security shop/api.py:37
    Path traversal / arbitrary file write: the `os.path.basename(report_name)` sanitisation was removed and `report_name` is now joined directly to `export_dir`. A name like `../../etc/cron.d/job` escapes the export directory, and an absolute name like `/etc/passwd` makes `os.path.join` discard `export_dir` entirely. The caller can therefore create or overwrite any file the process can write, with attacker-controlled `body`. `require_admin` limits who can reach this but does not make it safe (compromised admin account, or a name forwarded from less-trusted input).
    fix: Reject absolute paths and `..` segments, then resolve `os.path.realpath(os.path.join(export_dir, report_name))` and require `os.path.commonpath([real_export_dir, resolved]) == real_export_dir` before writing; ideally allow-list a single `team/filename` pattern.
[1] medium security shop/api.py:38
    `os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)` runs on the unvalidated path, so a traversal or absolute `report_name` also creates arbitrary directory trees outside `export_dir`. It executes before any containment check and leaves those directories behind even if the later `open` fails.
    fix: Call `makedirs` only after the resolved path is confirmed to be inside `export_dir`, and limit the allowed nesting depth (e.g. one team folder).
[2] low security shop/api.py:35
    The previous `safe_name.startswith(".")` check was dropped, so hidden files such as `.htaccess` or `finance/.env` can now be written. Names with an empty final component (e.g. `finance/`) also pass the `not report_name` check and then fail at `open` with an unhandled `IsADirectoryError` instead of the intended `ValueError("invalid report name")`.
    fix: Split `report_name` on `/` and raise `ValueError` if any component is empty, `.`, `..`, or starts with `.`.
[3] low bug shop/api.py:38
    If `export_dir` is an empty string (current working directory) and `report_name` has no folder, `os.path.dirname(path)` is `''` and `os.makedirs('')` raises `FileNotFoundError`. This call worked before the PR.
    fix: Only call `makedirs` when the dirname is non-empty: `parent = os.path.dirname(path); if parent: os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)`.
</untrusted_96653c8ffc9a>

## 🔍 PR Review — #4888

> This PR removes the `os.path.basename` sanitisation in `shop/api.py` and joins `report_name` directly to `export_dir`, which allows path traversal and absolute paths to write attacker-controlled content anywhere the process can write; `os.makedirs` also runs on the unvalidated path and can create directories outside the export directory. Changes are requested to validate and contain the resolved path before any filesystem operation. Lower-severity issues include the dropped hidden-file check, an unhandled error for names ending in `/`, and a regression when `export_dir` is empty.

⚠️ **Changes Requested** · 4 findings · confidence 88%

---

### 📄 `shop/api.py`

> 🟠 **HIGH** — _security_ at `shop/api.py:37`
>
> Path traversal / arbitrary file write: the `os.path.basename(report_name)` sanitisation was removed and `report_name` is now joined directly to `export_dir`. A name like `../../etc/cron.d/job` escapes the export directory, and an absolute name like `/etc/passwd` makes `os.path.join` discard `export_dir` entirely. The caller can therefore create or overwrite any file the process can write, with attacker-controlled `body`. `require_admin` limits who can reach this but does not make it safe (compromised admin account, or a name forwarded from less-trusted input).
>
> 💡 Reject absolute paths and `..` segments, then resolve `os.path.realpath(os.path.join(export_dir, report_name))` and require `os.path.commonpath([real_export_dir, resolved]) == real_export_dir` before writing; ideally allow-list a single `team/filename` pattern.

> 🟡 **MEDIUM** — _security_ at `shop/api.py:38`
>
> `os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)` runs on the unvalidated path, so a traversal or absolute `report_name` also creates arbitrary directory trees outside `export_dir`. It executes before any containment check and leaves those directories behind even if the later `open` fails.
>
> 💡 Call `makedirs` only after the resolved path is confirmed to be inside `export_dir`, and limit the allowed nesting depth (e.g. one team folder).

> 🔵 **LOW** — _security_ at `shop/api.py:35`
>
> The previous `safe_name.startswith(".")` check was dropped, so hidden files such as `.htaccess` or `finance/.env` can now be written. Names with an empty final component (e.g. `finance/`) also pass the `not report_name` check and then fail at `open` with an unhandled `IsADirectoryError` instead of the intended `ValueError("invalid report name")`.
>
> 💡 Split `report_name` on `/` and raise `ValueError` if any component is empty, `.`, `..`, or starts with `.`.

> 🔵 **LOW** — _bug_ at `shop/api.py:38`
>
> If `export_dir` is an empty string (current working directory) and `report_name` has no folder, `os.path.dirname(path)` is `''` and `os.makedirs('')` raises `FileNotFoundError`. This call worked before the PR.
>
> 💡 Only call `makedirs` when the dirname is non-empty: `parent = os.path.dirname(path); if parent: os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)`.
